newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields flat, crown stable at noon.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields flat, crown stable at noon.

text.p: Swedish debt yields were unchanged and the crown stable aginst the mark.

Dealers said the curve was flattening due to higher than expected Swedish inflation for April and a speech by Riksbank Governor Urban Backstrom saying there was no need at the moment to change the repurchase rate.
Swedish consumer prices rose 0.5 percent in April from March and 0.2 percent year-on-year compared to expectations of a 0.2 percent monthly rise and a flat yearly figure.
"Sweden Statistics is using a new method for calculating the CPI and that has increased uncertainity a bit. That is why we did not see any rise in T-bill rates," one dealer said.
The market was now awaiting U.S. CPI data.

Six month T-bill rate was up one basis point at 4.18 pct and the ten year bond yield was unchanged at 6.94 pct. The crown softened marginally to 4.4760 crowns against the mark versus 4.4700 crowns on Wednesday.
